question: When your cat ignores a slice of cake, it isn't being polite. Which of the basic tastes can cats not detect at all?
source_excerpt: cat Tas1r3 is an apparently functional and expressed receptor but that cat Tas1r2 is an unexpressed pseudogene

extra.why_interesting: Owners assume a cat that ignores cake is just picky or well-behaved. In fact the cat cannot taste sugar at all, which makes sense for a strict meat-eater. The player can reason it out from the five basic tastes.
extra.verification_notes: Cats' Tas1r2 sweet receptor gene is an unexpressed pseudogene, so they lack a functional sweet receptor (PLoS Genetics 2005).

explanation: Cats carry a broken copy of the gene for the sweet-taste receptor, so sugar tastes of nothing to them. A pure meat-eater never needed that sense.

question: A newborn Dalmatian puppy is missing the one feature the breed is famous for. What is it missing?
source_excerpt: Dalmatian puppies don't have their signature spots when they are born. Instead, they have a plain, solid-colored coat without any markings.

extra.why_interesting: Everyone pictures Dalmatians covered in spots, even as puppies, thanks to 101 Dalmatians. In reality the newborns are plain white, which gives a delightful 'really?' moment that is easy to reach.
extra.verification_notes: Dalmatian puppies are born plain white and develop spots after about 10 days to 2 weeks; no newer development contradicts this (https://www.dogster.com/lifestyle/are-dalmatians-born-with-their-spots/).

explanation: Dalmatian puppies are born pure white, and their spots only start appearing after about two weeks. So a real litter would look nothing like the cartoon.
